articleTitle: Test research on the kinetic characteristic of dust particles under different electric field
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: In this paper, a coaxial cylindrical electrode model was adopted to investigate the kinetic characteristic of different dust particles under strong electric field around insulators. The kinetic and deflection characteristics of different particles under different electric field were researched. The test results showed that the DC electric field had an greater effect on particles than the AC's because the electric field force under DC is much larger than the polarization force under AC; The different kinetic characteristic between particles was due to their different particle size and microstructure.

articleTitle: Optimal pulse width modulation for current source converter based static exciter
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: This paper presents a new optimal pulse width modulation (OPWM) technique for the current source converter (CSC) which is used as part of the static exciter. The reduction of total harmonic distortion (THD) of ac side line current is considered as the control objective of the proposed OPWM. This is formulated as an optimization problem in this paper, and particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is applied to solve the nonlinear transcendental equations. Furthermore, in order to make this CSC based exciter fulfill more roles than the traditional static exciter, a decoupled loop control technique is adopted to design a controller for this exciter. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed OPWM technique and the control strategy.

articleTitle: Survey on the impact of Electric Vehicles on power distribution grid
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) are developing increasingly in recent years due to many associated economic and environmental factors. When connected to distribution grid, EVs may be considered both as active loads and energy storage devices,which will have different and significant impacts on the distribution system. This paper surveys the present situation of the researches on these impacts. Other aspects such as effects on grid stability and effects when power system occurs fault are also included. The features and defects of existing studies are pointed out. The conclusion of this paper is available for reference to the research on the impact of EVs on distribution grid in the future.

articleTitle: Influence of GIS structure on propagation of electromagnetic waves of partial discharge
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Partial discharge process caused by GIS typical insulation defect is mainly analyzed in this study, and propagation properties of electromagnetic waves in actual GIS structure are investigated by applying FDTD algorithm and using real PD current signal as excitation source. The results show that great difference occurs between electromagnetic waves excited by PD actual current signal and that by ideal Gaussian pulse excitation and basin type insulator, shielding electrodes and three-phase common enclosure can affect the amplitude, frequency component and propagation mode of electromagnetic waves. The electromagnetic waves signal intensity is not necessarily proportional to its distance from discharge source; the proportion of frequency components is proportional to the diameter of GIS shell when it propagate in breakers.

articleTitle: An “load forecasting - dispatching” integration system for multiple boilers in thermal power plants
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: An improved integration system of multiple utility boilers is proposed in this study. Short-term load demand forecasting and load dispatching for multiple boilers are the two function blocks, they are modeled with Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Multi-objective Optimization Problem (MOP) respectively. In particular, the MOP is solved by a novel hybrid multi-objective optimization algorithm with a combination of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Extremal Optimization (EO) solutions, called “PSO-EO-MO”. Both the two function blocks have been developed to a integration system software based on real production data from a thermal power plant and have being running online on the spot with the procedure of production. The results illustrate the efficiency and applicability of the software and the software has got Software Copyright in 2010.

articleTitle: A study of the effect of global radiation and other factors on seasonal maximum frozen depth in the Tibetan Plateau
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: In this study, monthly average daily global radiation of 22 radiometric stations across the Tibetan Plateau were utilized to determine the coefficients of monthly Angström-Prescott's model for estimating global solar radiation from sunshine duration. Using the model, global solar radiations of another 116 meteorological stations across the Tibetan Plateau were estimated. Combined with frozen ground data measurement at 75 stations, global radiation effects on the maximum frozen depth of active layer were discussed. The result showed that the global radiation in cold season (from October to February the next year) had much influence on maximum frozen depth of the active layer. The relationship between them in three typical stations showed a marked negative correlation. As a whole, the maximum frozen depth of the active layer in nearly 80% of all investigation stations had the same relationship with the global solar radiation, while the others showed a positive correlation. This indicated that the maximum frozen depth of the active layer was the result of combined effects of several other factors other than global radiation. Of these influencing factors, such as global solar radiation, local latitude, longitude, altitude, air temperature in cold season, relative humidity, accumulation of precipitation in cold season, etc., only local latitude, altitude, global solar radiation and air temperature showed high correlation with frozen depth. Essentially, the influences of local latitude and altitude can be regarded as the effects of global radiation indirectly. As the local latitude and altitude influenced the distribution of global radiation, so the global radiation was an important affecting factor on the maximum frozen depth of the active layer.

articleTitle: On practical tracking of digital systems
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: In this paper we consider practical tracking of nonlinear time-invariant digital systems. Definitions of different kinds of practical tracking are introduced. Based on these definitions we give and prove criteria and control algorithms that ensure practical tracking. Simulations of the proposed control algorithms are performed, where a manipulator with three rotational joints (three DOF) is used as an object. The results of the simulation verify the proposed theory.

articleTitle: Nonlinear control of electronic power transformer for distribution system using feedback linearization
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: In this paper, a mathematical model of electronic power transformer for distribution systems (DEPT) is established, and a nonlinear control scheme is proposed for high performance control of DEPT. The proposed control scheme is based on the state feedback exact linearization technique developed based on differential geometry theory. With this control scheme, the dynamic responses of the system become very fast. The system is tested for dc-link reference voltage, load and input voltages variations respectively. The validity of the proposed model and control strategy is demonstrated by simulation results.

articleTitle: Adaptive control for grid-connected DFIG wind power generation system
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: A novel control strategy is presented for the back-to-back PWM converters of the grid-connected DFIG wind power system to enhance the transient performance and reliability of the overall system during physical parameter uncertainty and certain grid disturbance. The system description is modeled by using the field-oriented vector of the stator and voltage-oriented vector of grid control. The rotor-side and grid-side converter controllers are designed in integration by utilizing nonlinear adaptive control technology. The theoretical analysis shows that the proposed controller can guarantee the system to achieve the maximal absorption of wind power, constant dc-bus voltage, and constant voltage constant frequency output with respect to variable wind-speed, parameter uncertainties and disturbance. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is validated by the simulation comparison with the conventional PID controller.

articleTitle: Distribution network reconfiguration based on the minimum comprehensive cost with distributed generations
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: A new network reconfiguration approach with distributed generations (DG) is presented for minimum power loss and switches operation times in which the comprehensive cost is taken for objective function and the optimal structure of distributed network can be found through the improved adaptive GA. At the same time the coding method based on the loop is adapted which greatly reduces the infeasible solutions produced during genes algorithm operations in the application to distribution system reconfiguration. The test conducted on IEEE33-bus system has showed that the total profits were increased greatly with this method, and the power loss can be reduced, the voltage profile also increased.

articleTitle: Economical research of distribution network reconstruction in emigration areas
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Based on the difference between reconstruction and reconfiguration of distribution network, a mathematical model of distribution network reconstruction which sets minimal economic losses as its goal is presented. At last, three main options are made to achieve economic reconstruction of distribution network in general. Accordingly, the algorithm which regards minimize economic losses as heuristic information in the course of search on three major programs on specific examples is described, in order to find a distribution network of economic reconstruction programs and reduce distribution network reconstruction of capital investments.

articleTitle: Research on the current limiting scheme of the transformer-isolated multilevel H-bridges DSTATCOM
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: A current limiting scheme of the transformer-isolated multilevel H-bridges DSTATCOM is proposed. The novel scheme, based on the none zero seuence optimal algorithm, is able to compensate the negative sequence load current preferentially when the DSTATCOM capacity is not enough to compensate the full load current. Based on the current Limiting scheme, a holistic compensating scheme of DSTATCOM is proposed to make it adapt fluctuant load current. Finally a 2.5 Mvar DSTATCOM module is presented and the simulation results in PSCAD verify the validity and accuracy of the proposed current limiting scheme and the holistic compensating scheme.

articleTitle: Research on drive dynamics of hydraulic band sawing machine
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: In order to investigate sawing dynamics on band sawing machine, a general dynamic model is proposed to represent the actual system with the dynamics of strain of band saw, mechanism of hydraulic motor with proportional valve and load of sawing. Firstly, an element strain model of band saw along the arc coordinate is established with the elastic deformation theory of closed band saw, momentum theorem of band sawing element and sawing load. Then, the relationship between control input, sawing load and band saw tension is addressed with the dynamics of hydraulic motor with proportional valve. The results of dynamic simulations and experiments show the proposed model can effectively describe dynamics of band sawing process. This model provides a useful way to improve dynamics of band sawing.

articleTitle: The design of the super capacitor group used in heavy gantry portal cranes
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: In this paper, a system used super capacitor group to recycle the regenerative energy of the heavy gantry portal cranes is briefly introduced, which could save and reuse the energy generated during the download movements of the cargoes and the braking of the trolley, and be more friendly to the environment than the usual portal cranes. What's more the design method of super capacitor group is mainly presented. This method simplifies the calculations, and is easier to define the numbers of the parallel/serial capacitors compared to the usual try and error method.

articleTitle: Identification of leak zone pre-drilling based on fuzzy control
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: The key factor of plugging operation is how to identify leak zone as well as the difficult point for drilling operation in complex formation. Drilling fluids leakage and reservoir contamination frequently occurred due to the traditional method of identification of leak zone that lost circulation had already happened before detected. In this paper, the difficult problem of technology in identification of leak zone before drilling is solved by using fuzzy control theory. According to analyzing relevant parameters of lost circulation, the relationship between Euclid approach degree and lost circulation is established by using fuzzy relationship of lost circulation parameters. The field application indicated that this method is more accurate and workable in forecasting and practicing whereas the cost is effective. Above all, good results have been achieved in predicting the risk of leak zone by introducing this method.

articleTitle: Research on the deformation of transformer windings based on the analysis of short circuit reactance
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Windings deformation of power transformer during operation will cause a change of short-circuit reactance, therefore,we introduce the finite element method to calculate the transformer short-circuit reactance.In this paper, a model of power transformers is established by using software ANSYS,and transformer reactance parameters are calculated. The test results of ANSYS simulation indicate that the accuracy and correctness is high, and can provide a theoretical basis for the detection of windings deformation of power transformer.

articleTitle: A new and intelligent operation assessment system in simulation training of substation
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Most nation-wide substation simulation systems only provide the function of generating dispatch operation sheet and the new personnel always fail to cope well with the operation for the vital network and the complex dispatch task due to their lacking of practice and shortage of intensive memorization. It's necessary to enhance the training intensity while the new function should be implemented for optimizing in order to promote the training effectiveness. For above problems, the envisage design for the assessment system in this paper is presented based on self-invented substation simulation system of generating dispatch operation sheet.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation analysis of 3-level VSC-STATCOM based on SVPWM
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: This paper describes the modeling and analysis of a 3-level Static Synchronous Compensator(STATCOM) based on space vector pulse width modulation(SVPWM). The STATCOM is configured using a 3-level Voltage Source Converter(VSC). For high power applications the 3-level VSC is surpassed the commonly used two-level VSC in several aspects such as: harmonic components, dc link voltage and semiconductor devices switching frequency. It is important to keep the voltage constant in the power system, therefore voltage regulation is needed in the power system. VSC-based STATCOM regulate voltage in the connected bus by absorbing/supplying the required reactive power. The operating characteristics of the STATCOM is validated by simulation using PSCAD/EMTDC.

publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference

articleTitle: Transfer capability study of tie-line installed TCSC considering transient stability constraints
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: The transfer capability of tie-lines installed Thyristor Controlled Series Capacitor (TCSC) is studied in multi-machine systems considering transient stability constraints. Since the conversion time of TCSC mode has the important effect on transient stability, the discrete control strategy(DCS) is presented based on corrected transient energy function. The multi-machine system is divided up sending-end and receiving-end two equivalent machine systems. The moment just at which the corrected kinetic energy reach the maximum value is used as the start moment of TCSC maximum capacitive impedance in order to increase compensation degree, and the moment just at which the corrected potential energy reach especial value is used as the start moment of TCSC bypass mode in order to reduce short-circuit current. IEEE 4-generator system and New England 10-generator system are used as case studies, transfer capabilities of tie-lines considering transient stability constraints are calculated with the conventional control of TCSC and with the discrete control of TCSC, respectively. The calculation results show that the discrete control of TCSC enhances significantly the transfer capability of tie-lines in multi-machine system considering transient stability constraints compared with the conventional control of TCSC.

articleTitle: A design of generator excitation control based on NDAS model
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: This paper proposed the Modified Multi-Index Control (MMIC) design method in nonlinear differential algebraic system (NDAS), according to differential geometric control theory, M derivative, etc. Firstly, principle of this method is researched. Secondly, Based on Hartman theorem, c<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub> parameter in the method is configured in linear system. Besides, MMIC is applied to single machine infinite-bus power system, which is based on nonlinear differential-algebraic model, and excitation control scheme is proposed. Last, the simulation results demonstrate that the scheme can enhance the regulative precision of generator terminal voltage, and make states trace for their given values respectively. For the system with implicit function, dynamic and steady-state performance are coordinated effectively by the method. Thus, MMIC is valuable for application.

articleTitle: Study of the influence of UHVDC systems shared grounding electrode on the environment
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: This paper studies on the influence of grounding electrode shared by UHVDC systems on the environment. According to the design of grounding electrode shared by Yun-Guang UHVDC system and Gui-Guang II HVDC system, the neutral point current of transformers in nearby AC substations are given. The substations with neutral point current which exceeds the limit are listed. The paper also presents the neutral point current of the converter transformer caused by the underground DC current. The corrosion on the reinforcing steel bar inside a hydro power station nearby is analyzed. The influence of the underground DC current on the railway is also discussed.

articleTitle: Bifurcation analysis of maps with delay in nonlinear term via a frequency-domain approach
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: A unified frequency-domain approach to analyze Hopf and period-doubling bifurcations in nonlinear maps with delay is presented. The technique relies on the HBA (harmonic balance approximation) and feedback systems theory. The expressions of the bifurcation solution and the stability are obtained. One example is used to verify the result obtained.

articleTitle: Research of monitoring power quality applying CVT in the high-voltage power network
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Simulation of the CVT's harmonic measurement distortion, and the transformation ratio characteristics have been simulated by using the high-frequency equivalent circuit.The relationgship between the main stray capacitance's change and the change of CVT's pass band have been analyzed. At the same time, combining the engineering application, we propose to make use of the combination of experimental data with artificial neural network to correct the CVT's transformation ratio. This method can be used to monitor harmonic chronically through the CVT. Testified by emulators, this method is feasible.

articleTitle: Study on LVRT capability of D-PMSG based wind turbine
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Wind power in China is experiencing rapid development in recent years, and problems come forth due to the grid connection of large-scale wind power. Based on the status of wind power development in China, necessity of wind farm low voltage ride through (LVRT) capability is studied in this paper. The strategy for LVRT realization of D-PMSG based wind turbine is presented by studying the control system of wind turbine, and the control processes during LVRT period is showed. A study case is given to show the impact on power grid when wind farm is with or without LVRT capability and also to show the validity of LVRT models and control system presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Notice of Retraction: Fault diagnosis of marine boiler superheater tube rupture based on fuzzy neural network
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: This article has been retracted by the publisher.

articleTitle: Research on design of brushless doubly fed generator
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Brushless doubly fed generator(BDFG) is attractive with the development of wind power generation. This paper focuses on the design of BDFG. After representing the configuration and principle, the design procedure of BDFG is studied, three different types are analyzed using FEA particularly, and the rotor with the best coupling capability is selected. These analyzed conclusions will lay the foundation for BDFG application.

articleTitle: Design and realization of power quality monitoring system based on B/S model
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: With the development and application of Web technology, the power quality (PQ) monitoring system is providing a new application platform for large-scale information share. It will simultaneously increase efficiency while greatly decreasing workload. The software with three-tire B/S (Browser/Server) structure needs to administer only the server, so all the clients are just the browsers and do not need any maintenance. In this paper, the three-tier system structure model of PQ monitoring system, the structure of the application servers and the data exchange standards PQDIF (PQ date interchange format) are discussed. The GUI of the Application Server and the PQDIF file in XML are also given.

articleTitle: Communication of the wind turbine testing system based On CANopen protocol
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: On the basis of analyzing the structure and characteristic of CANopen protocol, this article emphasizes on the realization way of how to establish data communication of the wind turbine testing system with CANopen protocol. In this paper, the speed, torque and other communication parameters of the wind turbine testing system have been designed, built and programmed in details. Finally, the reliability of data communication system is testified by experiment.

articleTitle: AC/AC converter with the Z-source and high frequency link
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: This paper proposes a high frequency AC/AC converter based on Z-source, which is composed of input filtering circuit, inductor, input cycloconverter, high frequency transformer, output cycloconverter, control switch and output filter. The paper gives in-depth the steady-state principle and control strategy of the circuit. Finally, the simulation and experimental results show that the converter has the merits of output transformation, frequency conversion, high frequency electrical isolation, bidirectional power flow, load adaptability, etc. And it lays a key technique foundation for Intelligent Universal Transformer (IUT), sinusoidal AC voltage stabilizer, voltage regulators, and power compensator.

articleTitle: Computer control system of 550mm experimental mill for hot flat rolling
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: This paper describes in detail the equipment, the process, the configuration of the computer control system, the control strategy and the algorithm of gauge control system in experimental mill for hot flat rolling. Two-stage computer control system is used. They are respectively basic automation system and process control system. The process parameters, such as gap and plate thickness, can be accurately controlled by the automatic control system. Practical application shows that the system has the characteristics of reasonable structure, reliable performance, high control precision and perfect function.

articleTitle: Optimal switch for a common system
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: A common system consists of the same creatures or the same model man-made machines, and the power consumption of this system includes several factors. The optimal switching method is given for this system, and the minimum total power consumption is given also.

articleTitle: Integral control of hospital environment
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Hospital presents a complex indoor environment. Patients, healthcare workers/staff and visitors can not be treated as uniform group with the same needs, demands and conditions for thermal comfort. There is no method or system to provide optimal thermal comfort for everyone besides rational energy use for heating and cooling. The paper presents a design of a smart patient room in which thermal comfort conditions are highly controlled and energy use for heating and cooling minimized. Control system is based on the concept of individualization of personal space. With this respect two systems for heating and cooling are compared on the basis of thermal comfort calculations for two patients and measured energy use for heating and cooling. Human body exergy balance model is used together with building energy model. To control HE a smart system on the basis of fuzzy logic is applied. An individualized personal zone is designed.

articleTitle: Research on the burial depths of the annular grounding electrodes in UHVDC converter stations
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: The grounding electrodes of UHVDC power grid can constrain continuously neutral voltage of the converter stations, and protects equipments from damaging as unbalanced voltage. Therefore, it is important to improve the feature of the grounding electrodes. This paper focus on the domestic ±800KV DC annular grounding electrodes features. Based on the equivalent image method, to double annular electrodes buried in uniform soils, the effects depending on the burial depth of the grounding electrodes are analyzed. Through calculating and simulating, the results show that the step voltage and the earth resistance decrease with increasing the depth of the Grounding electrodes, but the temperature of the Grounding Electrodes increases. The project of unequal burying depth of the Grounding Electrodes such as inner being lighter than the outer is proposed, and the best laid proportional range of the inner and outer ring is proposed also. These projects improve grounding features and security to UHVDC power grid, and decrease engineering quantity.

articleTitle: Mechanical monitoring and risk assessment under ice disaster based on wireless sensor network
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Ice disaster has becoming a significant threat to power system security since recent years. Wireless sensor networks guarantee reliability of information communication under ice disasters, due to their self-organization and the advantage that master stations are not involved. It is recommended to be applied on power grid structure security monitoring and assessment. It is proposed that different type of sensor nodes should be settled on overhead transmission lines, to comprehensively monitor mechanical status of a certain area. A two-layer sensor network model is presented for overcoming the communication range limitations of sensor nodes. Using the data obtained, a novel power system financial risk assessment method is proposed to balance the probability and seriousness of icing caused supports break, which helps grid structure progress in a long term.

articleTitle: Conceptual design of a novel de-icing device for power transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: The technique regarding de-icing and anti-icing for power transmission lines is very important since severe ice storms may cause disaster to power grid due to influence of the accreted ice. In this paper, a novel de-icing device with fixed function position for power transmission lines is proposed. The possibility of mechanical de-icing methods and the features of fixed function position are given to show the advantages of the proposed de-icing device. In particular, the structure of the de-icing device and the function principle are described. The proposed de-icing device would enhance the customer service and benefit power companies and line maintenance companies.

articleTitle: Electric field analysis of 220kV composite rod insulator
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: In the power transmission equipment, insulator is an important outer insulator part. It is used in electric insulator and machine fixedness. Composite insulator owns some advantages, such as: lighter weight, easy maintenance, etc. It is widely used in high voltage power transmission. In order to understand the insulator characters, this paper uses finite element method to analysis its electric field distribution, based on acquaint the insulator structure characteristic of 220kV composite insulator. First mathematics model of composite insulator is constituted. Then the ANSYS soft is used to calculate it. In the end, some calculated results are analyzed. Some conclusions are got. In this kind of insulator, the most uneven electric strengthen lies in two sharp ends of insulator, as same as it is easiest to appear part-discharge. This conclusion has practical instructional meaning to the usage of this insulator. The analysis method using in this paper can widely applied in more complicated condition of various insulator's electric field analysis.

articleTitle: NOx removal in the selective non-catalytic reduction (SNCR) process and combined NOx and PCDD/Fs control
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: NOx removal from flue gases by selective non-catalytic reduction (SNCR) was investigated with special attention paid to combined dioxin destruction in waste incineration plants. For the SNCR technology, ammonia (NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) and urea-based reductants are widely adopted, and the important factors affecting De-NOx efficency associated with SNCR were investigated here, including the effective temperature range, normalized stoichiometric ratio (NSR) of NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (or urea)/NOx. However, NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> slip and N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O emissions are the two common problems related with the SNCR process and operating conditions should be delicately designed for their control. With respect to combined dioxin control in De-NOx process, the technology is mainly related to selective catalytic reduction (SCR) since the effective temperature range for SNCR is away from the dioxin formation temperature zone. But there was also investigation showing that the SNCR process based on hydrazine hydrate exhibited some dioxin reduction. In order to control PCDD/Fs effectively, and to prevent NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> slip and N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O emission in the SNCR process, it is suggested that the reagent corresponding to lower SNCR effective temperature range should be investigated.

articleTitle: Two-switch three-level discontinuous conduction mode boost rectifier design
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Front-end converters for distributed power system (DPS) applications are extensively used in telecommunication systems to supply load converters and to charge batteries to provide backup energy during power grid blackouts. This paper explores the main features of the two-switch three-level boost rectifier operated in discontinuous conduction mode (DCM). The main contributions are reduced voltage stress and improved efficiency. Control strategies and design guidelines are provided in this paper. Because of the voltage stress reduction brought about by using a three-level topology, MOSFETs can be used to simultaneously increase the switching frequency and efficiency of the power factor correction (PFC) circuit. The discussion is supported by simulation results obtained from a 6.3kW prototype.

articleTitle: A new approach for comparing communication infrastructures of power systems
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Power system communication infrastructures are responsible for data transmitting among different entities in power systems. System data and information (provided by sensors) are crucial for monitoring, operating and controlling reasons. On the one hand, real-time and near real-time processes of power systems utilize communication infrastructure for sharing their information. On the other hand, power system sensors and actuators are distributed in wide geographical area and they belong to communication system. Consequently, some network parameters e.g. communication delay and reliability; which may be not essential in other communication systems; have become a major concern in power system communication infrastructures. This study aims to propose a method for comparing any given power system communication infrastructures in terms of latency (delay) and reliability. The simulation results indicate that although two communication networks may be similar in the view of cost and service, our proposal method can recognize reliable communication network with better latency condition.

articleTitle: Analysis of transformer short circuit characteristics based on 3-D Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Based on a 3-D Finite Element Model built up in FLUX 3-D, this paper shows simulation results of a single phase transformer to study the behavior of its reactance during short circuits with respect to saturation effects. In the first step measurements on a real transformer were done to determine its equivalent circuit parameters and to verify the Finite Element Model. In the second step the influence of core saturation on the impedance was studied. From the result of this study it can be concluded that the saturation has a big impact on the maximum short circuit current and has to be taken into account for detailed network studies.

articleTitle: Risk-based maintenance schedule of transmission line using multi-objective evolutionary algorithm
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: This paper describes a risk-based approach for multi-objective maintenance schedule of transmission line. A novel risk index is calculated by probabilistic load flow method, which accounts for the fluctuation of generator power, loads and transmission line's outages. Elitist non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) is used to find the optimal solutions in large search space. The test results on the Roy Billinton Test System (RBTS) demonstrate the validity of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A research of the fractal dimension based on GIS PD signals in time domain
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: This paper introduced the definitions of box dimension and information dimension, and analyzed the characteristics of these dimensions. In this paper the fractal dimensions of GIS partial discharge (PD) signals in time domain for the fault of immobilized metal particles attached to insulator surface were calculated, the variation-trend and relevant characteristics of related dimensions at different discharge stages were analyzed. This paper proposed that with the development of partial discharge, distribution of fractal dimension have a significant transformation, and by analysis of the changing of these two dimensions at different voltage level, the development of PD in electrical equipment could be assessed, this is has great significance to the assessment and diagnosis of insulation condition about electrical equipment.

articleTitle: New general method for digital differential protection relay
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: In This paper, computational aspects of a digital transformer differential relay is described. DPFC percent differential protection reflects deviation of load condition which can perform a sensitive protection for the transformer. The ability of Inrush Current Detection with Waveform Distortion Discrimination Principle is discussed and demonstrated. Test results of the proposed algorithm highlight the abilities of the algorithm. Test results for external fault, internal fault and inrush current are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Simulation study on temperature rising for the traction convertor of high-speed EMUs
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Traction convertor plays a main role to ensure the power of High-Speed EMUs. The temperature rising of the convertor directly impacts the reliability of the operation of EMUs and the life time of the convertor. This article analyses the power loss of the convertor, establishes the temperature rising model under the conditions of the cooling system, and designs the simulation software for temperature rising by taking the example of CRH3 High-Speed EMUs. This software monitors the temperature of the main parts of the traction convertor in the process of the EMUs operation, which provides the scientific basis for power configuration and the features of the temperature rising.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of integrated gasifier-solid oxide fuel cell power plants with different system configurations
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: It is desirable to use renewable fuel sources for solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) for future combined heat and power (CHP) generation. Biosyngas from biomass gasification is a candidate thanks to the sustainability and the practical carbon neutrality of the biomass resources. Performance of integrated gasifier-SOFC power plants with two different fuel cell system configurations is presented. The integrated system includes a downdraft fixed-bed gasifier, a gas cleaning system and a SOFC CHP system. Anode outlet gas recirculation is employed in one configuration and direct fuel delivery to the anode without recirculation is employed in the other. The results show that system configuration influences the system performance. The integrated system with a direct biosyngas delivery to the fuel cell stack has higher system efficiencies with 21% for the net AC electrical efficiency, 54% for the total CHP system efficiency and 22% for the system exergy efficiency, while the system with ejector-driven anode recirculation gives lower net AC electrical efficiency of 13%, the total CHP system efficiency of 49% and the system exergy efficiency of 15%.

articleTitle: Analysis and prediction on wind power in provincial grid
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Along with the increasing of the capacity of wind power, load-following regulation has become the main factor that restricts the power grid's acceptance ability of the wind power. This paper presents a method and model for predicting the acceptance of wind power energy from the aspect of load-following regulation, aiming to provide an intuitive demonstration of the power grid's acceptance ability of the wind power and guidance for the planning and dispatching of wind power. Based on the present condition of the gird, composition of power source and the actual operational data of 2010 of the Northern Provinces of China with a rich wind power resource, this paper calculate and predict the provinces' acceptance of wind power energy in 2011 in detail under different scenarios. Suggestions for increasing the wind power in the system are presented.

Author Keywords: predicting the acceptance of wind power energy

articleTitle: Study on the total electric field at the ground level under two circuit DC transmission lines in the same corridor based on the upstream FEM method
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: The erection of two circuit DC transmission lines in the same corridor can increase the power transmission capability of the unit corridor, however, there still have been no engineering application precedents in the world for the construction of two circuit DC transmission lines in the same corridor. The situation of parallel adjacent erection for Xiangjiaba~Shanghai and Jinping~Sunan ±800kV DC transmission lines will appear in some sections in China, it is necessary to study the valid calculation method for their total electric field at the ground level to satisfy the requirements in engineering design and environment protection. In this paper, a calculation method for the total electric field was proposed which is based on the Upstream FEM Method, and its validity was proved by test results. The results of calculation and test were obtained and shown as follows. The different pole arrangement schemes of two circuit DC transmission lines in the same corridor would not notably influence the magnitude of the maximum total electric field at the ground level, but would influence its distribution location. The absolute value of the maximum total electric field at the ground level under two circuit DC transmission lines in the same corridor is not greatly different from that of just one circuit in normal operation.

articleTitle: Fault diagnosis of transformer based on cluster analysis
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: In order to solve the problem of the imbalance between the fault data and the normal ones in the fault diagnosis of transformer, we adopt k-means algorithm to cluster the data. The result of clustering shows the existence of the boundary class that is between fault and normal ones. The separation of boundary class from the fault data and the normal ones improves the reliability and early warning ability of fault diagnosis of transformer, as well as reduces the influence from the imbalance of the two kinds of data.

articleTitle: Wide area damping control with continued data-packet losses in the communication
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Solution of wide area damping control is presented in the paper. The speed difference between generators is used as wide area supplementary stabilizing signal. The communication delay is compensated by lead-lag network. A method to determine the optimal location and number of wide area damping controllers (WADC) is given. The fitness function for optimization algorithm is an integral of time-weighted squared errors. The continued data-packet losses in the communication are resolved by prediction using least squares support vector machines. The simulation of a 10-machine 39-bus power system shows that WADC can improve the stability of interconnected power systems.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation of DC/AC converter for wind power flow optimization based on instantaneous reactive power theory
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: In the wind power flow optimization control system, 3-phase DC/AC converter is used to realize two-way flow of active power and reactive power, of which the key problem is that how to realize decoupling control of active current and reactive current. Traditional d-q decomposition method makes the design of control system complicated. In order to simplify the design of control system, p-q decomposition method is proposed based on instantaneous reactive power theory, which is used to establish 3-phase DC/AC converter's mathematical model. The simulation using Matlab/simulink shows the feasibility of the modeling method.

articleTitle: Non-fault detection for single-phase reclosure of transmission lines based on fault location
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: It is important to study on non-fault detection before reclosing for single-phase reclosure, which is helpful to lower unsuccessful reclosing rate and meet the increasing requirement on self-healing ability in smart grid. Some researchers have developed single-phase long-hold faults identification criterion based on differential current principle, for the open phases in faulting and non-fault are considered as internal fault and external fault respectively. But the distributed capacitive current compensation is influenced by the fault location. Especially in the case of the fault location near to bus at each side of the transmission line, the capacitive current compensation method is not effective for the distance side. Therefore, a distributed capacitive current compensation based on fault location is discussed for non-fault detection of single-phase reclosure. ATP simulations show that the developed criterion based on fault location is of higher sensitivity and reliability.

articleTitle: Controller fine tuning of a human brachial artery system prototype (static model)
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: In this paper, controller for a human brachial artery system prototype is formulated with respect to a static model. Operational procedure of the designed prototype has been highlighted. Because of linearity of the designed system, major components (pump and shaker) are considered autonomously during preliminary analysis. Ziegler - Nichols tuning methods and pole placement scheme have been utilized to calculate the controller parameter values. At the concluding stage, the computed values for pump and shaker are combined to denote the overall response of the system. Simulation results have been presented to verify the correctness of the utilized techniques. It has been concluded from obtained results that the determined controller parameter values for both pump and shaker are more than satisfactory for all three typical test inputs.

articleTitle: Design of the bus active speed control system based on ARM
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: From the bus active safety standpoint, this article designs the embedded system to control the speed of automobile in time without changing the original structure. The system selects STR712FR2 based on ARM7 as the microprocessor, able to control the automobile speed in accordance with the road conditions. The system has advantages in simple structure, low power consumption and practical function. The system function, the overall design and implementation procedure of the system, the software and hardware choice are analyzed in detail. Meanwhile, the initial validation of the system is carried out.

articleTitle: Research on ancillary service management mechanism in the smart grid
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Smart grid have flexible demand response patterns, adapt to multiple energy generation forms, diversify and decentralize energy supply, intellectualize energy storage ways and coordinate operation between transmission and distribution grids and micro-grid. This paper analyzes the effect of renewable energy generation, distributed generation and large scale demand response on ancillary service, and quantify reserve and peak shaving capacity when implementing Interruptible Load Management and Time-of-Use. The example results show the consumer side is equal to generation side. In the end, this article preliminarily suggests that developing smart grid should make full use of the existing resources, and firstly enhance power demand side management and improve the interaction between consumers and power grid to improve grid's ability of accommodating renewable energy and efficiency of using electrical power resources.

articleTitle: Research on the describing of trajectory for subsea pipeline based on Inertial Navigation System
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Due to the variance of seabed geology appearance, it is difficult to provide accurate and real time geographic information for shallow sear subsea pipelines. Therefore, it is impossible to locate the defects of the pipelines; leading to the reparation hard to be performed. The describing of trajectory and location of defects based on INS (inertial navigation system) will be discussed in this paper. By analyzing the longitude and latitude location of the pipeline route, the relative locations of defects on the inner surface of pipelines to the geographical coordinate system can be determined. Error analysis and correction were done based on the results of laboratory testing. Field tests were also performed for offshore oil pipelines and results showed that the acquired data met errors requirements. Analysis and experiments results proved that using INS to solve the defect location and pipeline trajectory describing were accurate and feasible.

articleTitle: H∞ robust control of DC-AC interfaced microsource in microgrids
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: This paper focus on the DC-AC interfaced microsource system based H∞ robust control strategies. First, it presents detail of a model of DC-AC interfaced microsource which is connected to the power grid through a controllable switch. Then, select the double loop control scheme for the dc-ac interface. In case of the load disturbance and the model uncertainties, the inner voltage and current loop is produced based on the H∞ robust control strategies. The outer power loop uses the droop characteristics controller. Finally, the scheme is simulated using the MATLAB/SIMULINK. The simulation results demonstrate that DC-AC interfaced micro-source system can supply high quality power. Also, it is established that the proposed control scheme can make the system smooth switching between the isolated mode and grid-connected mode.

articleTitle: Research on bogie stiffness test control strategy for six-dof hydraulic servo loading plate
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: In order to improve test equipment of domestic high-speed train bogie, a fuzzy five states control strategy base on phase plane is presented aiming at the tracking control problem of electro-hydraulic servo position control system with uncertainties and nonlinearities. The results of simulation show that the control approach can overcome the nonlinear problem of the hydraulic system, has nice robustness, and improve tracking accuracy considerably.

articleTitle: Simulation of traction transformer based on PSCAD / EMTDC
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: This paper introduces the structures and the principles of three typical models of traction transformer in railway traction power supply system. Through the simulation based on PSCAD / EMTDC, the results show that these models of the traction transformers are reasonable. Furthermore, the traction power supply systems based on autotransformer (AT)model with three traction transformers are simulated respectively in this paper. Also, this paper focuses on the Catenary voltage distribution and the voltage on the train in these traction power supply systems. Compared the theoretical values with the simulation values of these traction power supply systems, the results show the advantages and disadvantages of three traction transformers, and verify the validities of these traction power supply system models which meet the engineering requirements.

articleTitle: Design optimization of GIS circuit breaker based on RBFEM
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Along with the structural miniaturization of GIS, electric field distribution becomes more complex in GIS. It is an urgent demand to instruct the insulation design of electrical equipment by using reliable and effective numerical computational method and technology to calculate its three-dimensional electrical field. In this paper the RBFEM (Reduced-basis FEM) is introduced. The principle of RBFEM is analyzed. The order of reduced-basis matrix is much smaller than the number of nodes, and its sets of data values cover the entire regime including all FEM solutions. The novel algorithm is applied to design the shape of arc-quenching chamber of GIS circuit breaker. Owe to compute the reduced-basis matrix the computational effort can be cut down without significantly affecting the accuracy of the FEM solution.

articleTitle: Recovery of steam produced from a large scale medical waste incinerator boiler: Choice of utilization system
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Steam generated from boiler in medical waste incinerator is seldom used due to its production and parameters are unstable. In this paper, three different utilization systems, namely power generation with adoption of condensing steam turbine, co-generation and combined cooling heating and power system (CCHP) of steam generated from the heat recovery boiler of 72t/d medical waste incineration in a hazardous waste disposal center are discussed respectively. The result shows that the CCHP may be a good choice taking into account cooling in summer and heating in winter in Shanghai. In the system of CCHP, when selecting the type of B1.03-2.1/0.3 back-pressure turbine, the generated energy is 1030kW, refrigerating quantity is 7668kW in summer and heating output is 18105kW in winter. Additionally, the effect of steam parameter fluctuations on the generation power is discussed.

articleTitle: Resistance against external aggression for central tube submarine optical fiber cable
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: The central tube submarine optical fiber cables (SOFC) with double armors are recommended to lay in shallow water. However, they are often damaged by external aggression. The finite element method (FEM) models of two cable types, which are double-armored cable and single armored cable with two inner armors, are proposed in this paper. Crush and snag resistance performance of the cables are compared and analyzed. The distortion and strain of cable's tube core are simulated by the FEM model. Simulation results verified that the performance of inner armored cable is better than that of double armored cable.

articleTitle: A heuristic model for scheduling wind turbines
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Due to variability of electricity price, grid demand and wind speed as well as heterogeneity of wind turbines, operators of a wind farm encounter challenges of determining operational status of wind turbines (on/off) to achieve power generation objectives but minimize the total cost. A heuristic model that develops scheduling strategies of wind turbines for operators in a wind farm is discussed in this paper. A modified particle swarm optimization algorithm with small world network structure is introduced to solve the heuristic model. The computed scheduling strategies suggest the operational status of wind turbines over the pre-determined scheduling horizon that minimizes the total cost of a wind farm.

articleTitle: Design and application of dual-redundancy excitation mode in AVR of aero-generator
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: A technique of dual-redundancy excitation mode in AVR of aero-generator is designed in this paper. PWM proportional excitation mode is used in main voltage regulation and oscillating excitation mode is used in backup voltage regulation. Aided excitation improves the performance of voltage buildup on the basis of self-excitation. The question of Aided excitation in practical application is analyzed and the solution is given. Experiments validate the performance of dual-redundancy excitation mode.

articleTitle: The determination and correction of measurement anomaly based on wavelet-threshold method
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: The malfunction of measuring apparatus is almost inevitable in electric system and will result in inaccurate settlement amount of electricity sales. The backup measures, such as dual-apparatus, calculations from the measurement on other side of line or Tele Meter Reading of EMS are helpful to rectify the erroneous data. It has to detect the anomaly according to the inherent character of load as those back-up absent. A method of determination and correction of measurement anomaly based wavelet-threshold is proposed in this paper. It decomposes the measurement data in multi-scale space with wavelet transform and determines the scale-coefficient which includes the anomaly data based on the difference between normal load fluctuation and extraordinary error. A modified threshold function is used to separate the error component from the scale-coefficient. The correction component can be reconstructed from the error component in the binary tree of wavelet transform. An example is given to test and verify the method finally.

articleTitle: Reduction of load model based on perturbation method
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: This paper describes the concept of the multi-time scales in math and derives a integrated typical model that represented by the induction motor. Then the system is separated to some subsystems in different scales for the purpose of reducing the order of the model. Finally the perturbed models for induction motor are developed, implemented and tested on the one-machine infinite-bus system. The dynamic performances of the perturbed models are compared with the full models as well as the simple models which completely neglect fast transients during simulations. From the simulation results it is seen that the perturbation technique is reasonable.

articleTitle: Calculation on induced over-voltage on low-voltage overhead lines
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: There are always very tall buildings next to the low-voltage transmission lines through the city centers. If the buildings are stroke directly by lightning, the extremely high transient electromagnetic field caused by lightning current through the lightning downward lead might induce high over-voltages on the low-voltage transmission lines. If the induced lightning over-voltage exceeds the withstanding ability of the insulators, lines will flashover to the cross arm of the tower. In this paper , the equation used to calculate the induced over-voltage on the low-voltage overhead transmission lines less than 65m far away from the lightning stroke point is deduced and the sensitivity studies are carried out to indicate how the parameters would influence induced over-voltage.

Author Keywords: distance from the lightning stoke point

articleTitle: Reducing grounding electrode step voltage by installing underground insulating layers
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: This paper introduces a method to reduce the step voltage of grounding electrode. The method is able to reducing the step voltage without changing the design plan or increasing the electrode size. The financial cost of this method is low. By installing an insulating layer on the top of the grounding electrode, the leakage currents are forced to flow into the deeper layer of soil. Therefore, the step voltage values on the surface near the grounding electrode are reduced. By applying a numerical method, the efficiency of the method is analyzed and a field experiment is conducted to verify the effect of the method.

articleTitle: Optimal Design and Characteristic Analysis of magnetic array levitation system
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: In this paper, a 3-degree of freedom levitation system is proposed, which contains the electromagnet array and the permanent magnet. The mathematical model is built, and the whole structure is optimized from three aspects, as magnetic force, controllability and resultant magnetic field. The efficiency of the new electromagnetic system is better than the traditional one. The characteristics and the synthetic magnetic properties of the magnetic suspension force are analyzed based on the finite element method. The experimental results show that the suspension system designed can be used for the large air gap with good stability and control.

articleTitle: Simulation and synchronization studies on voltage collapse model in power system
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Dealing with power system became one of the most important arts in the field of power system, especially in the rapid increase of the distributed generation (DG) penetration to the distribution level which is a vital and important part of the entire power system. In this paper, a very special power system on voltage collapse model has been studied. We will establish its synchronization behavior. We investigate the chaos synchronization of two identical systems based on nonlinear observer. Control laws are derived analytically to achieve synchronization of the chaotic fractional order system which appling this voltage collapse model to a simple 3-bus power system model. Numerical simulations are provided to verify the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: SMES device and its power control strategy
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: Compared to other energy storage form, SMES has prominent advantages. It is a mature superconducting power device in the power system. It owns a promising application prospects. This paper introduces operating principle, basic structure, the application in power system and other aspects about SMES. In addition, on the basis of understanding its different component parts, its core function, control strategy of power regulate is elaborated. A new effective improvement PWM control method is mentioned.

articleTitle: Fast solution algorithm for optimal placement of distributed generations
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: A novel method for optimal placement of distributed generations has been proposed in this paper. The proposed method takes the minimization of active power losses of distribution network as optimization objective, and determines the optimal location of distributed generations by order of the sensitivity factor of power losses respective to bus loads, then calculates the optimal capacities of distributed generations by the solution of a set of linear algebraic equations which is derived by use of the mathematical extremum value principle. The proposed method is clear and brief, very fast in computation. This method has been tested on IEEE 33-bus distribution system, and the simulation result has shown that the proposed method is efficient.

articleTitle: A scheme to control neutral point voltage variation in three-level converter
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: The three-level technology of converters has the weak point of the neutral point voltage potential unbalance. This paper describes a scheme to control neutral point voltage variation in three-level converter. The scheme solves the problem by controlling the three-level rectifier. The parameters in it can be reconstructed and it avoids adding complexity to the inverter. The simulation at the last part demonstrates validity of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: A novel on-line measuring system of temperature for power system electric contact
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: The temperature sense system of photonic crystal liquid crystal fiber grating used on temperature measure for power system electric contact is presented based on the narrow band filtering of the photonic crystal fiber(PCF) and helix liquid crystal pitch sensitive to temperature. The system is consisted of the broadband optic source, liquid crystals filling photonic crystal temperature sensor, fiber filter, signal amplification and amplifier, and display module. The electric contact temperature may be real-time measured based on the wavelength of the maximum optical power point change of photonic crystal which the helix liquid crystals filled in, wavelength changed represented by fiber filter, the relation of liquid crystal pitch with temperature, and data processing. The sense system is special suit to the power system electric contact temperature on-line detection as it has the perspective of the intrinsically safe, high precision, high electrical insulation and anti-electromagnetic interference.

articleTitle: A control strategy of three-phase active power filter with unity power factor
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: The control strategy of three-phase active power filter is discussed base on one-cycle control technology. No matter how the source voltages are balanced or unbalanced, the control strategy of active power filter can be determined by calculating the unbalanced parameters of the source voltages and determining the duty ratios of switches in phase. With this control strategy, the active power filter can make the source currents in-phase with the source voltages which can results in unity power factor of the system. Finally the simulation of the control strategy is made, and the results of simulation show that active power filter with this control strategy can effectually compensate the harmonics and make the losses of switches reduced. Because it does not need harmonics checking circuit, the control circuit is simple and has capacity of fast following.

articleTitle: H∞ control of time-delay state feedback Markovian jump linear systems with uncertain transition rates
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: This paper deals with the H∞ time-delay control problem for a class of uncertain Markovian jump linear systems (MJLSs). Since it's difficult to obtain the transition rates of real control systems, we consider the systems with uncertain transition rates. Combining H∞ control theory, we propose a sufficient robust stochastic stability criterion of the system. Then, the H∞ time-delay state-feedback controller that makes the underlying system stabilizable with γ-disturbance attenuation is designed. By constructing a Lyapunov functional, the time-delay independent LMI-formatted globally stability criterion is proposed based on robust control theory. Then, numerical example is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the derived results.

articleTitle: Sampling data preprocessing subsystem for integrated protection
publicationTitle: 2011 IEEE Power Engineering and Automation Conference
abstract: This paper designs a novel sampling data preprocessing subsystem in integrated protection based on IEC61850. This subsystem will be used to solve the problems of data redundancy processing and bad value processing. A framework structure of integrated protection software system based on the concept of module distributed is firstly presented, and then the details of preprocessing subsystem are given. This subsystem is the most important foundation of integrated protection. It can provide a platform to analyze and validate the protection arithmetic. Meanwhile, the subsystem will reach the requirement for security, real-time and reliability.
